title: Cache Warming Strategies
description: Learn how to pre-populate a Redis cache before high-traffic events to avoid cold-start penalties and cache stampedes.

data.text: **Cache warming** is the practice of loading data into a cache before it is requested by users. A cold cache — one that has just started, been flushed, or never received a particular key — forces every request to hit the database until the cache fills up. Warming eliminates that cold-start penalty by pre-loading the most important keys.

Warming is especially important before predictable traffic spikes: Black Friday sales, product launches, or scheduled report generation. It is also useful after Redis restarts, RDB restores, or deployments that flush the cache.

terms.definition: Pre-loading data into a cache so that user requests find a warm, populated cache instead of an empty one.
The period when a cache is empty or missing critical keys, causing requests to fall through to the database.
A caching strategy that serves expired data while refreshing it in the background.

data.title: Common Triggers
items: **Application startup** — Load reference data like countries, currencies, or feature flags.
**Pre-deployment** — Before swapping traffic to a new version, warm caches so the first users do not trigger a stampede.
**Scheduled events** — Load product catalogs, pricing, or inventory before a sale goes live.
**After Redis failover** — Re-populate critical keys after a node replacement or promotion.
**CI/CD pipelines** — Seed caches in staging environments so integration tests behave like production.

data.text: The simplest technique is a **warming script** that iterates over a list of known hot keys and writes them to Redis. More sophisticated systems use a **warming service** that runs continuously, keeps track of key popularity, and refreshes entries before they expire.

data.title: Warm incrementally
data.text: If you have millions of keys, do not try to warm them all at once. Warm the top 1% of hot keys, then use background jobs to gradually fill in the rest.

**Stale-while-revalidate** is a variation where you continue serving an expired cache entry while a background job fetches fresh data. The user never waits for a cache miss, and the cache updates itself asynchronously. This pattern is popular in CDNs and HTTP caches, but it also works for Redis when combined with a lightweight background scheduler.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Cache warming pre-loads hot keys so users never hit a cold cache.
Warm on startup, before deployments, and before predictable traffic spikes.
Use batch operations to warm efficiently without overwhelming Redis.
Combine warming with TTL and jittered TTLs for a robust caching strategy.
data.takeaway: Warming turns Redis from a reactive cache into a proactive one — be ready before the traffic arrives.
